item.title: GovBrief Today #660
item.description: Donald Trump ordered every federal contractor to call the White House before answering questions from Congress. The order he signed Friday night covers tens of thousands of businesses and the subcontractors working for them. Each one must report any request from Congress about its government work, then follow White House instructions on what to hold back. A company that answers anyway can lose the contracts it has and be barred from winning new ones. That same day, the Pentagon's inspector general opened an audit of the department's deals with defense start-ups. Democrats had asked for one after The Washington Post found that companies tied to Trump's two oldest sons collected $3.2 billion in Pentagon money. On Jan. 3 those Democrats take control of Congress. Any company they contact must now tell the White House first, and the White House decides what it is allowed to say. On February 1, 2025, I typed a list of nine things I never imagined a government doing in one day and sent it to my family. I've sent one every night since: 10,051 stories over 660 straight nights, free and without ads. Add your email address at the website and I'll send it to you too. NEW: Zoom In is now live! Our first interactive focuses on how Kilmar Abrego Garcia was wrongly deported and his unsettled future. https://go.govbrief.today/abrego-garcia-timeline [1] https://go.govbrief.today/iran-war-nov21 [2] https://go.govbrief.today/miller-usn [3] https://go.govbrief.today/ice-seatac [4] https://go.govbrief.today/contractors-wh [5] https://go.govbrief.today/nc-wells [6] https://go.govbrief.today/homelessness-grants https://gbounacos.substack.com

item.title: MapQuest Is Fighting The System By Showing Flock Camera Locations To Drivers
item.description:
Before Google Maps and Apple Maps appeared on smartphones (and then in cars), people would have MapQuest work out a customized route on the PC, which you then needed to print. While Google and Apple eclipsed MapQuest, it never went away. Recently, MapQuest has been deliciously rebellious by refusing to acknowledge certain body of water name changes by President Trump. And now, the company is documenting known mass surveillance devices you might encounter on your journeys, including cameras from Flock. MapQuest Doesn't Capitulate To Authority If you haven't used MapQuest but have heard of it recently, it's likely because of its satirical response to President Trump signing an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. Not only did MapQuest not capitulate and change the name of the Gulf of Mexico on its maps, it announced a new website called "Name Your Own Gulf" to allow people to, well, name their own gulf on a map. When Google Maps and Apple Maps renamed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users, MapQuest didn't – and became the most downloaded app on the iPhone App Store in the United States on September 1. Now, as Halloween is being promoted as DeFlock America night, MapQuest's new Surveillance Layer in Map Options reveals known license plate readers from Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), Genetec, Axis Communications, Axon, Leonardo (ELSAG), Neology, Rekor, PlateSmart, Ubicquia, Verkada, and more. How Does MapQuest Know Where The Mass Surveillance Devices Are? MapQuest declared in a post on Bluesky that "The Roads Have Eyes!" and showed the surveillance layer with the cameras represented by animated eyes and the location of the user represented as a ghost.
